plan: Mirror Dense004's proven approach: reproduce the NATIVE torch.compile (Inductor) weighted-SwiGLU math exactly in Triton with FP32 interior arithmetic and single round-to-BF16 stores, so optimized stays inside atol 3e-4 / rtol 1e-3 against weighted_bias_swiglu_impl(input,None,weights,False) for output, input_grad AND weights_grad. No change to GEMMs, router, loss, dtype, dataset, baseline fusion, tolerance or timing.

Public entry weighted_swiglu(x, weights, *, native): fast path only for CUDA BF16 contiguous x[dim 2/3, even last dim] with BF16 contiguous weights[N,1] whose N == flattened token count; everything else (CPU, FP32, non-contiguous-incompatible, dtype/shape mismatch) delegates once, unchanged, through the supplied native callback passing the exact (x, weights) objects — satisfying the CPU/FP32 guard probes with zero native_fallback_calls on supported shapes.

Forward kernel (flattened over the H-sized output, H:tl.constexpr, BLOCK=1024, num_warps=4): a,b = BF16 gate/up loads .to(fp32); w = weights[row] load .to(fp32); sig = tl.sigmoid(a); y = ((a*sig)*b)*w; single BF16 store. This is exactly native swiglu(y)*weights then cast — one rounding. row=offs//H, col=offs%H, gate=row*2H+col, up=gate+H covers every even and odd H (257/769/2048).

Backward input_grad kernel on the SAME H-sized flattened grid: gg = g_fp32 * w_fp32 first (native swiglu_back(g*weights,y)); sig=tl.sigmoid(a); tmp8=gg*sig; tmp10=1-sig; tmp11=a*tmp10; tmp12=tmp11+1; tmp13=tmp8*tmp12; dx_gate=tmp13*b; dx_up=gg*(a*tl.sigmoid(a)); two BF16 stores, writing both halves per program with no duplication — identical FP32 op order to the audited Dense004 backward with g replaced by g*weights.

Backward weights_grad kernel: one program per row, BLOCK=next_power_of_2(H) reduction; recompute swig=((a*sig)*b) in FP32, summand=swig*g_fp32 (native swiglu(y)*g.to(weights.dtype)), s=tl.sum(summand,axis=0) in FP32, single BF16 store to dw[row]. If the Triton tree reduction ever drifts from Inductor's it stays well within tolerance; the native-Torch reduction remains the sanctioned fallback behavior without changing semantics.

torch.autograd.Function saves (x, weights) only; forward allocates a fresh (prefix,H) BF16 out; backward calls g.contiguous(), allocates fresh dx=empty_like(x) and dw=empty_like(weights) every call. numel==0 returns the empty out / empty dx,dw with no launch (no grid or divide-by-zero math). Nothing cached is ever a result or a pinned tensor/pointer/stream.

Dispatch cache holds ONLY immutable CompiledKernel launch closures, keyed per phase by (device, exact numel, H, grid, next-pow2 BLOCK, num_warps, data_ptr()%16 of every tensor arg). Hit: call the closure with CURRENT runtime args (constexpr H/BLOCK dropped); the closure fetches the active stream each launch, so fresh inputs on non-default streams stay correct. Miss: kernel[grid](args, H=H, BLOCK=..., num_warps=...) launches and the closure is stored. Exact-numel keying keeps equal_to_1/div-16 specializations from ever crossing closure classes; %16 alignment keying distinguishes odd-storage-offset views.

Guarded closure reuse (vendor Triton 2.1 constexpr-runner arity unverified): the first closure-call failure flips a global flag, clears the cache, and all later calls use the plain kernel[grid] miss path — correctness never depends on the closure working, and a re-launch after a closure miss is idempotent (same inputs overwrite identical outputs). No enable_fp_fusion / fp_fast_math kwargs; imports limited to torch, triton, triton.language; no file/network/process/env/seed/hardcoded-input access.

Promotion gate unchanged: fresh full-MoE numerical admission (router probabilities/maps and probability gradients included), then control = CE0008+gradnorm001 and optimized = control plus only this candidate; 120 steps with first 20 discarded across seeds 34102/34103/34104; promote only if strictly >1% incremental throughput vs same-round control AND faster on every one of the three seeds, else keep native weighted SwiGLU. No production/GroupedGEMM/multi-GPU/convergence claim.
risks: Closure arity for H-constexpr kernels in vendor Triton 2.1.0 is unverified; if closure(x,w,out,numel) / closure(x,g,w,dx,numel) / closure(x,g,dw) does not accept these runtime args, every launch falls back to the plain kernel[grid] path — correct but with no dispatch savings, so the >1% gate may not be met.

weights_grad uses a Triton per-row FP32 tree reduction rather than Inductor's reduction; the summand and op order match native exactly but the summation association can differ by a ULP. It stays inside atol 3e-4 / rtol 1e-3 here, yet is the single most likely source of drift across the 4-layer full-training admission, where native Torch reduction is the sanctioned fallback if needed.

Matching Inductor bitwise-closely still depends on the vendor compiler emitting the identical FP32 sequence and one round-to-nearest BF16 store per output; any auto-inserted intermediate cast or reassociation could reintroduce the 1-ULP divergences that broke earlier dense attempts, risking the formal numerical gate.

data_ptr()%16 plus exact-numel keying is conservative (many closure classes under alternating expert token counts N=38..256 and odd-offset views), which can dilute the cache-hit benefit without harming correctness.

int32 offset arithmetic is safe for the declared shapes (max gate offset for N=256,H=2048 is ~2.1M < 2^31) but would overflow for much larger inputs; this candidate targets only the observed moe-weighted shapes.

The closures preserve native per-launch stream fetch; if any harness path pins a stream around the module hook, parity on the two fresh-input non-default-stream probes must be re-confirmed. No tolerance, timing, baseline-fusion or dtype weakening is introduced to compensate.

tail widths with BLOCK=next_power_of_2(H) (H=257->512, H=769->1024, H=2048->2048) rely on the masked reduction zeroing lanes >= H; a miscount would corrupt weights_grad, but mask=offs<H with other=0.0 covers it for every probed width.
